title: The Shift to Multiplayer Work: Say Hello to Slackbot’s MCP Client | Slack

facts.fact: Slack's blog post announcing the Slackbot MCP client is dated June 17, 2026, and its headline says users can work with over 20 partner applications that integrate with Slackbot and shared channels.
facts.quote: Now you can work with over 20 partner applications that integrate with Slackbot and shared channels

facts.fact: Slack states it is launching a partner ecosystem of more than 20 MCP apps, naming Amplitude, Atlassian, Box, Canva, Docusign, Gamma, Linear, Miro, Notion, Replit, Webflow, and Zoom, with more on the way.
facts.quote: launching a partner ecosystem of more than 20 MCP apps, including Amplitude, Atlassian, Box, Canva, Docusign, Gamma, Linear, Miro, Notion, Replit, Webflow, and Zoom, with more on the way.

facts.fact: Slack states that its Slackbot Model Context Protocol (MCP) client is now generally available.
Slack states the MCP client respects Slack's native compliance, security infrastructure, and permission controls out of the box.
facts.quote: The MCP client respects Slack’s native compliance, security infrastructure, and permission controls out of the box.

facts.fact: Slack states the system applies user-specific data boundaries in real time, so a user without credentials for a restricted database is not given access to it.
facts.quote: The system applies user-specific data boundaries in real time: If someone doesn’t have credentials for a restricted database

facts.fact: Slack claims (vendor claim, not independently verified) that connecting a custom tool through MCP takes minutes, whereas custom integration development previously could take months.
facts.quote: Instead of dealing with months of complex development, your team can bring your tools to life inside Slackbot in minutes.

facts.fact: Slack states that partner tools can render rich visual components, including data tables and interactive carousels, inside Slackbot threads using its Block Kit framework.
facts.quote: Partner tools can now render rich visual components, including data tables and interactive carousels, directly inside your threads using the Block Kit framework.
